terms.gloss: loose, too big (of a shoe or a garment)
evidence: Hor. S. 1.3.31–32: male laxus in pede calceus haeret
Lewis & Short: of a toga, Tib. 1.6.40
terms.comment: The plain word for a shoe or garment that is too big; nimis laxus of clothes.

phrases.latin: ut calceus ōlim, sī pede major erit, subvertet, sī minor, ūret
phrases.english: like a shoe: too big it trips you, too small it pinches

phrases.latin: Haec tunica tibi nimis laxa est; mox apta erit.
phrases.english: This top is too big for you; soon it will fit.

phrases.latin: toga dēfluit et male laxus in pede calceus haeret
phrases.english: his toga slips down, and his shoe, far too loose, barely stays on his foot

sources: Lewis & Short: laxus
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. loose.
